speaker: Unknown
en: Data retrieval is a fundamental challenge in AI systems, and the approaches for solving it are still evolving.
zh: 数据检索是 AI 系统中的一项根本性挑战,解决它的方法仍在不断演变。

speaker: Unknown
en: Vector search was an early answer to the retrieval problem, but the rise of agentic systems has raised the stakes considerably.
zh: 向量搜索是检索问题的早期答案,但智能体系统的兴起让这个问题的利害关系大幅提升。

speaker: Unknown
en: Agents issue queries at machine speed, decompose complex questions into parallel searches, and require retrieval infrastructure that can keep pace without becoming prohibitively expensive.
zh: 智能体以机器速度发出查询,把复杂问题分解成并行搜索,并且需要能跟得上节奏又不会贵得离谱的检索基础设施。

speaker: Unknown
en: Chroma is a company building open-source infrastructure for AI applications, best known for its widely used database of the same name.
zh: Chroma 是一家为 AI 应用构建开源基础设施的公司,以其广受欢迎的同名数据库而闻名。

speaker: Unknown
en: The company also published the Influential Context Rot paper, which documented how model performance degrades as context window utilization increases, and recently released Context 1.
zh: 该公司还发表了颇具影响力的 Context Rot 论文,记录了模型性能如何随着上下文窗口利用率的增加而下降,并最近发布了 Context 1。

speaker: Unknown
en: A 20 billion parameter retrieval sub-agent trained to do agentic search at frontier model quality but at an order of magnitude lower cost and higher speed.
zh: 这是一个 200 亿参数的检索子智能体,经过训练能够以前沿模型的质量执行智能体搜索,但成本低一个数量级、速度更快。

speaker: Unknown
en: Hamad Bashir is the CTO of Chroma, with a background spanning machine learning, computer vision, and data systems.

speaker: Unknown

zh: 在本期节目中,Hamad 与 Gregor Vann 一起讨论 ChromaDB 的起源、我们目前对 context rot 的理解、为什么一个专门构建的小模型能在搜索任务上匹敌前沿模型、Chroma 开源方式背后的理念,以及公司如何看待 AI 数据基础设施的未来走向。

en: I think it's a product that probably a lot of our audience are familiar with and probably familiar with these types of products as well.

speaker: Unknown
en: But before we get into that, I'd just love to hear, as we like to, Hamad, you've worked at quite a few interesting companies, I think in the Bay Area and beyond.

en: What's your quick path to getting to Chroma and all that?
zh: 你快速讲讲你是怎么一步步走到 Chroma 的?

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, I spent better part of the decade as a software engineer and broad expertise in machine learning, computer vision, and data systems was most of what I worked on for the past decade.
zh: 好,我把这十年里的大部分时间都花在了软件工程师的工作上,机器学习、计算机视觉和数据系统方面的广泛专长是我过去十年工作的主要内容。

speaker: Unknown
en: And before this was spending a lot of time specifically on computer vision.
zh: 在此之前,我专门花了很多时间在计算机视觉上。

speaker: Unknown
en: And initially when we started on Chroma, the problem that we were solving is one of active learning for computer vision systems, which is the problem of every day you have a bunch of live deployed computer vision systems.
zh: 最初当我们开始做 Chroma 时,我们要解决的问题之一是计算机视觉系统的主动学习,也就是每天你有一堆线上部署的计算机视觉系统时,如何主动标注你在真实环境中看到的数据。

speaker: Unknown
en: How do you actively label the data that you're looking at in the wild?
zh: 以及挑选哪些数据值得标注。

speaker: Unknown
en: And select which data is worth labeling.
zh: 因为如果你把所有数据都标注了,成本会高得无法承受。

speaker: Unknown
en: Because if you label everything, it's cost prohibitive.
zh: 所以选择哪些数据来标注的过程,是一个训练时的数据筛选问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that process of choosing what data to label is a train time data curation problem.
zh: 而随着语言模型开始兴起,我们开始在推理的语境下审视这个问题,也就是你如何真正为模型筛选数据供其推理使用。

speaker: Unknown
en: And as language models started to emerge, we started to look at that problem in the context of inference, which is how do you actually curate data for models to do inference on.
zh: 具体到语言模型,这就是搜索问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: And specifically language models, this is the problem of search.
zh: 你如何真正找到最相关的数据来提升其回答质量?

speaker: Unknown
en: How do you actually find the most relevant data to enhance the quality of their answer?
zh: 而这正是我们如今在 Chroma 构建的工具栈——一套帮助人们为其下游 AI 应用开发搜索功能的工具,以便他们能把正确的信息或正确的上下文送进他们的语言模型。

speaker: Unknown
en: Which is the stack of tools that we now build at Chroma is a stack of tools to help people develop search for their downstream AI applications so that they can get the right information or the right context into their language models.
zh: 是的,很好。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, nice.
zh: 那么,很有意思的背景,引出了你们现在在 Chroma 所做的一切。

speaker: Unknown
en: So yeah, interesting background leading into like how, I guess, everything that you guys are now doing at Chroma.
zh: 也许先来一个简单的介绍。

speaker: Unknown
en: Maybe just a sort of easy introduction.
zh: 什么是 Chroma?

speaker: Unknown
en: What is Chroma?
zh: 这个产品有几个部分,但大致来说,Chroma 是什么?

speaker: Unknown
en: There's a few bits to the product, but like roughly speaking, what is Chroma?
zh: Chroma 的核心,是试图解决让模型获得它们所需上下文的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: So Chroma, at its core, is trying to solve the problem of getting models the context they need.
zh: 为此,我们在平台中构建了三个主要的技术组件,人们可以把它们组合起来解决这个问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: And to that end, we build three main pieces of technology in our platform that people can put together to solve that problem.
zh: 其中核心是大多数人使用的产品,也就是我们的核心数据库,即 ChromaDB。

speaker: Unknown
en: The core of it is the product that most people use, which is our core database, so ChromaDB.
zh: 它目前是与语言模型配合使用的最广泛使用的数据库之一。

speaker: Unknown
en: Which is now one of the most widely used databases in conjunction with language models.
zh: 它的作用是,你可以非常轻松地把数据导入其中,并使用多种不同的搜索技术——向量搜索、全文搜索、元数据搜索——来获取可能与语言模型相关的信息。

speaker: Unknown
en: What it does is you can very easily ingest data into it and use a variety of different search techniques, vector search, full text search, metadata search, in order to get information that might be relevant to a language model.
zh: 与之配套,我们还有一个产品部分叫 Sync。

speaker: Unknown
en: In conjunction with that, we also have a part of our product we call Sync.
zh: 它是一个托管的 ETL 管道,用于把来自各种来源的数据导入那个数据库。

speaker: Unknown
en: Which is a managed ETL pipeline for ingesting data from various sources into that database.
zh: 这是一个托管的 ETL 管道,用于把来自各种来源的数据导入那个数据库。

speaker: Unknown
en: We found that most developers don't want to be building that sort of a pipeline themselves because putting data into a search database requires a lot of processing.
zh: 我们发现,大多数开发者并不想自己构建那种流水线,因为把数据放进搜索数据库需要大量处理。

speaker: Unknown
en: You have to clean the data, you have to transform the data in a way that makes it vectorizable so you can search it.
zh: 你得清洗数据,你得把数据转换成可向量化的形式,这样你才能搜索它。

speaker: Unknown
en: You ideally want to enrich that data with metadata.
zh: 理想情况下,你还想用元数据来充实这些数据。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that process is quite cumbersome to do in a high throughput way.
zh: 而且要以高吞吐的方式完成这个过程相当繁琐。

speaker: Unknown
en: So our sync product solves that.
zh: 所以我们的同步(sync)产品就是解决这个问题的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then quite recently, earlier this year, we launched a product we call Context 1.
zh: 然后就在最近,今年早些时候,我们发布了一个叫做 Context 1 的产品。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's mostly a research endeavor and we're in the process of productionizing it.
zh: 它主要是一个研究项目,我们目前正在把它产品化。

speaker: Unknown
en: What it is is a model that does agentic search.
zh: 它本质上是一个执行智能体搜索的模型。

speaker: Unknown
en: So agentic search is the process of instead of a language model application, just doing a single search and then putting that search into the context window directly, a process commonly known as RAG or retrieval augmented generation.
zh: 所谓智能体搜索,就是语言模型应用不再只做一次搜索、然后直接把那次搜索结果放进上下文窗口——那个过程通常被称为 RAG,即检索增强生成——

speaker: Unknown
en: What you can now do is tell a language model
zh: 而是现在你可以告诉一个语言模型

speaker: Unknown
en: Please take this query, perform a multiple set of queries, take some high-level English query, turn it and decompose it into a set of low-level queries against some search system, and then repeat that process until you feel comfortable with your end conclusion.
zh: 请拿这个查询,执行多组查询,把一个高层次的英文查询分解成一组针对某个搜索系统的低层次查询,然后重复这个过程,直到你对最终结论感到满意为止。

speaker: Unknown
en: Kind of the way you and I would sit down and answer a query.
zh: 有点像你和我坐下来回答一个问题时的方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: We wouldn't type something into Google, look at the first 10 links, and then say, my job is done.
zh: 我们不会在 Google 里输入点东西,看看前 10 个链接,然后就说,我的任务完成了。

speaker: Unknown
en: We would read some documents, author more queries, read some more documents, author some more queries, follow the links on those pages, and do exhaustive research.
zh: 我们会读一些文档,再写更多查询,再读更多文档,再写更多查询,顺着那些页面上的链接,做穷尽式的调研。

speaker: Unknown
en: The models now do that process themselves.
zh: 现在模型们自己完成这个过程。

speaker: Unknown
en: However, it's quite cost prohibitive to do with large frontier models.
zh: 然而,用大型前沿模型来做这件事的成本相当高昂。

speaker: Unknown
en: So context one is a model that was trained using reinforcement learning to be just as good at frontier models at this process, but at an order of magnitude less cost and an order of magnitude more speed.
zh: 所以 Context 1 是一个用强化学习训练出来的模型,它在这个过程上的表现和前沿模型一样好,但成本低一个数量级,速度快一个数量级。

speaker: Unknown
en: So compared to Opus 4.6, we run at around 400 tokens per second, 500 tokens per second, whereas something like an Opus would run at around 40 to 80 tokens per second.
zh: 相比 Opus 4.6,我们以每秒约 400 个 token、每秒 500 个 token 的速度运行,而像 Opus 这样的模型运行速度大约是每秒 40 到 80 个 token。

speaker: Unknown
en: So the end result is that you get your answers at the same quality much, much faster and for much, much cheaper.
zh: 所以最终的结果是,你以同样的质量、快得多、也便宜得多地得到你的答案。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we're going to go into context one a bit later on.
zh: 我们稍后会深入聊 Context 1。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we're going to hear all the interesting detail of, I guess, how that actually works in practice.
zh: 到时候我们会听到所有有趣的细节,我猜,关于它在实际中到底是如何运作的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I think just looking at Chroma generally, when I first came across this space, vector search was such a big thing for a while.
zh: 所以我想整体看看 Chroma,当我刚接触这个领域时,向量搜索曾经火了很长一段时间。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then at least in my framing, it kind of disappeared for a while.
zh: 然后至少在我的印象中,它消失了很长一段时间。

speaker: Unknown
en: But now it's coming back in what I feel is quite a big way.
zh: 但现在它以一种我觉得相当大的方式回归了。

speaker: Unknown
en: So if we kind of start there, like I guess the journey of Chroma from its founding, I guess, or when you came into Chroma and what were you working on at the start and like how has that evolved?
zh: 所以我们就从这里开始聊吧,我猜是 Chroma 从创立以来的历程,或者说是你加入 Chroma 的时候,你们最初在做什么,以及它是如何演变的?

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 好的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So as I mentioned, what we were working on at the very beginning was how do you choose what data is worth retraining models on?
zh: 正如我提到的,我们最初在做的是,如何选择哪些数据值得用来重新训练模型?

speaker: Unknown
en: So the problem of, hey, every day my models do some tasks out into the world.
zh: 也就是这个问题,嘿,每天我的模型都会到外面的世界里执行一些任务。

speaker: Unknown
en: At the time it was actually computer vision models.
zh: 当时其实还是计算机视觉模型。

speaker: Unknown
en: And some subset of that data is worth relabeling for the process of what's called active learning.
zh: 而这些数据中有一些子集是值得重新打标签的,这个过程叫做主动学习(active learning)。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it turns out that that same process can be used for language models at inference time.
zh: 而事实证明,同样的过程也可以用于语言模型的推理阶段。

speaker: Unknown
en: So how do you actually choose what data to put into the context window while you do search and you find related information the same way that you might find related information when choosing what data to label at train time?
zh: 也就是在执行搜索时,你如何实际选择要放进上下文窗口的数据,找到相关信息的方式与你在训练阶段选择要打标签的数据时找到相关信息的方式相同?

speaker: Unknown
en: That was the initial problem that we went out to solve.
zh: 那就是我们最初要解决的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: And actually the way we went about solving it was using existing vector search solutions.
zh: 而实际上,我们解决它的方式是使用现有的向量搜索方案。

speaker: Unknown
en: We didn't set out wanting to build a database.
zh: 我们最初并没有想要构建一个数据库。

speaker: Unknown
en: But what we found is that every other solution on the market was quite poor in terms of serving the workload that AI applications had.
zh: 但我们发现,市面上所有其他方案在服务 AI 应用的负载方面都相当糟糕。

speaker: Unknown
en: Specifically, systems that were built for legacy search, not for AI applications, were really designed around the idea that you have one very large index.
zh: 具体来说,那些为传统搜索而非 AI 应用构建的系统,实际上是围绕「你只有一个非常大的索引」这个理念设计的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you might have a billion pieces of information to search over or a million documents to search over.
zh: 也就是说,你可能要有十亿条信息可以搜索,或者一百万份文档可以搜索。

speaker: Unknown
en: But they're all in one index.
zh: 但它们全都在一个索引里。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if you want to add another half a million, what do you have to do?
zh: 而如果你要再增加五十万条,你得做什么?

speaker: Unknown
en: You have to recharge your cluster.
zh: 你得重新给集群充容。

speaker: Unknown
en: You have to add a node, subtract a node, rebalance across those nodes, which is a very manual and operationally intensive process.
zh: 你得增加一个节点、删减一个节点、在这些节点之间重新均衡,这是一个非常手动且运维密集的过程。

speaker: Unknown
en: AI applications have an almost opposite workload.
zh: AI 应用的负载几乎正好相反。

speaker: Unknown
en: Where instead of one or a handful of very large indices, you have extremely partitioned indices.
zh: 它不是拥有一个或少数几个非常大的索引,而是拥有极度分区的索引。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you might have an index per customer, an index per team, an index per chat history, an index per agent.
zh: 所以你可能每个客户一个索引,每个团队一个索引,每个聊天历史一个索引,每个智能体一个索引。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that means that your system has to be able to store a very, very large volume of unique indices and be able to search over them with a high degree of accuracy.
zh: 这意味着你的系统必须能够存储数量极其庞大的独立索引,并且能够以很高的准确度对它们进行搜索。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if you're to store all of those in one index, one, you have to pay the cost of keeping that live at all times.
zh: 而如果你把所有这些都放进一个索引里,第一,你必须承担让那个索引随时保持在线的成本。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then two, you have to deal with the accuracy degradation in vector search when everything is in one index.
zh: 第二,你还得应对所有东西都放进一个索引时向量搜索的准确度下降问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: Vector search doesn't do well with being partitioned.
zh: 向量搜索在被分区的情况下表现不佳。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so the best thing to do is hard partition the data, keep it actually in logically separate indexes.
zh: 所以最好的做法是对数据进行硬分区，把它们真正保存在逻辑上分离的索引中。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can't filter the search at query time.
zh: 你不能在查询时对搜索进行过滤。

speaker: Unknown
en: You have to do it at index time.
zh: 你必须在构建索引时做这件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so if your data has this partitionable structure, you can build many, many indexes.
zh: 所以如果你的数据具有可分区的结构，你就可以构建非常非常多的索引。

speaker: Unknown
en: And instead of needing to build one giant index, you get a much higher quality and cost trade-off.
zh: 而且不需要构建一个巨大的索引，你会得到质量与成本之间好得多的权衡。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so that's actually why we started to build Chrome with a database is because nothing else solved that problem for us in a high quality way.
zh: 这正是我们开始构建带数据库功能的 Chrome 的原因，因为没有其他东西能以高质量的方式为我们解决这个问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the core of it was at the time object storage.
zh: 它的核心在当时是对象存储。

speaker: Unknown
en: So Amazon has S3 and GCP has GCS.
zh: 亚马逊有 S3,GCP 有 GCS。

speaker: Unknown
en: Azure has their own thing.
zh: Azure 有他们自己的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: All started to release support for conditional rights, which is a new thing, especially on AWS.
zh: 它们都开始发布对条件写入的支持，这是一个新事物，尤其是在 AWS 上。

speaker: Unknown
en: It only came out as recently as 2024.
zh: 它直到 2024 年才推出。

speaker: Unknown
en: And conditional rights allow you to actually build a database on top of object storage.
zh: 条件写入让你能够真正在对象存储之上构建一个数据库。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so what we did is leverage that functionality in order to be able to build our database, ChromaDB, on top of object storage so that the economics would be something that make applications for AI actually viable.
zh: 于是我们所做的就是利用这个功能，以便能够在对象存储之上构建我们的数据库 ChromaDB,这样其经济性才能让 AI 应用真正可行。

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown

zh: 是的，我认为，我的意思是，任何智能体搜索框架的标准范式就是你只想给模型两个工具，一个是允许它搜索，第二个是允许它获取它看到的结果。

speaker: Unknown

zh: 如果你使用任何编码智能体，在上下文窗口的末尾，它会对自己的上下文进行总结或压缩。

speaker: Unknown
en: Our belief was that for leveraging a small model, this would be a very difficult endeavor.
zh: 我们的信念是，对于一个利用小模型的方案来说，这会是一件非常困难的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: It would be quite lossy.
zh: 它会有相当大的信息损失。

speaker: Unknown
en: You would potentially lose valuable information.
zh: 你可能会丢失有价值的信息。

speaker: Unknown
en: You might lose context if you're being dispatched by a larger agent in a narrow fashion.
zh: 如果你在一个狭窄的方式下被一个更大的智能体派遣，你可能会丢失上下文。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so how could we avoid any lossiness in the small model due to its inefficiencies and its inaccuracies?
zh: 那么，我们如何能避免小模型由于其低效和不准确而带来的任何信息损失呢？

speaker: Unknown
en: The idea that we came to is, can we just have it edit its context as it goes?
zh: 我们想到的主意是，能不能让它在自己进行的过程中编辑自己的上下文？

speaker: Unknown
en: So we give it this prune chunks tool.
zh: 所以我们给了它这个 prune chunks 工具。

speaker: Unknown
en: And doing agentic search is a very token heavy process because every document that you touch you end up loading into the context window and you very quickly process a very large volume of tokens very quickly.
zh: 做智能体搜索是一个非常消耗 token 的过程，因为你接触到的每个文档最终都会加载进上下文窗口，你会很快地处理非常大量的 token。

speaker: Unknown
en: What we do is we give it this tool that allows it to go back and remove documents from its own context window.
zh: 我们做的是给它这个工具，允许它回过头去从自己的上下文窗口中移除文档。

speaker: Unknown
en: And this is a trade-off between KVCache coherency and the overall token usage.
zh: 这是 KVCache 一致性和整体 token 用量之间的权衡。

speaker: Unknown
en: And what we found is the model is quite good at making judgments about relevancy and removing prior information from its own context window, which is not all that surprising in hindsight because the model already has to make that judgment in order to be successful at its task.
zh: 而我们发现，这个模型在判断相关性以及从自己的上下文窗口中移除先前信息方面相当擅长，事后来看这并不那么令人惊讶，因为模型本来就必须做出这种判断才能成功完成它的任务。

speaker: Unknown
en: The fundamental problem that you run into though is sometimes a document early on in the search rollout appears to not be relevant but then later becomes relevant.
zh: 不过你遇到的根本问题是，有时在搜索 rollout 早期的一个文档看起来不相关，但后来变得相关了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so a lot of the subtlety of training the model becomes how do you actually train it on a wide enough variety of cases that have a wide enough variety of problems that have different amounts of relevancy in the documents that it returns?

zh: 你如何能扰动它返回的文档，以便为模型创建足够有挑战性的示例？

speaker: Unknown
en: Such that it's trained to be very accurate in when it prunes.
zh: 使得它被训练成在何时进行剪枝这件事上非常准确。

speaker: Unknown
en: So when we trained Context 1, the base model is actually GPTOSS 20B, so it's a 20 billion parameter model.

speaker: Unknown
en: And when we trained it, initially the accuracy of pruning I think was around 80%.
zh: 而当我们训练它时，最初剪枝的准确率我记得大概在 80% 左右。

speaker: Unknown

zh: 也就是 80% 的时间它选择了正确的要移除的文档。

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown
en: So that ability to self-edit the context ends up leading to a very large reduction in the overall token usage.

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown

zh: 而我们也开始着手研究，你能不能真的把延迟作为一个训练目标？

speaker: Unknown
en: And so that it kind of learns the most optimal pruning strategy, not from an accuracy perspective, but also from a latency perspective.
zh: 这样它就能学到最优的剪枝策略，不仅从准确率的角度，也从延迟的角度。

speaker: Unknown
en: So there's all these subtle tricks you have to do in order to make it work.
zh: 所以为了让它工作，你必须做所有这些微妙的技巧。

speaker: Unknown
en: But fundamentally, I think the core contributing idea on the harness side of the model, the thing, the set of tools it has and the way that the model behaves is this idea of self-editing its own context and self-editing its own history.
zh: 但从根本上说，我认为在模型框架这边，核心的贡献性想法——也就是它拥有的那套工具以及模型行为的方式——就是这种自编辑自己的上下文和自编辑自己的历史的理念。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think if we just like look at how, like what the result of this is, I think it was stated that Context 1 at 20B matches, this isn't that long ago, so Opus 4.5, Sonnet 4.5, Gemini 3.1, Pro, and sort of most of your benchmarks.

speaker: Unknown
en: That seems pretty impressive.
zh: 这看起来相当令人印象深刻。

speaker: Unknown
en: It has an understatement.
zh: 这还是一种轻描淡写。

en: So I mean like, what's kind of your read on why a purpose-trained small model can actually get there, I guess?

en: I think the core belief is if you start to decompose what a model does when it searches,
zh: 我认为核心信念是，如果你开始分解模型在搜索时做的事情，

zh: 所以存在一个你可以遵循的程序，或者说一个你可以遵循的算法来执行搜索。

speaker: Unknown
en: And a lot of the time that algorithm is a set of very narrow tasks chained together.
zh: 而很多时候，那个算法是一系列非常狭窄的任务链接在一起。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if you can just figure out the right time to deploy those tasks, and if you can figure out how to be good at those subtasks, then you can be good at agentic search.

speaker: Unknown
en: Fundamentally, I think the set of tasks is how do I look at a high level user query and then decompose it into a plan of lower level queries to issue against the search system?
zh: 从根本上说,我认为这组任务就是:我如何查看一个高层次的用户查询,然后把它分解成一个由低层次查询组成的计划,并对搜索系统发出这些查询?

speaker: Unknown
en: How do I look at a page and determine its relevance?
zh: 我如何查看一个页面并确定其相关性?

speaker: Unknown
en: How do I look at a page and determine what follow-up queries to make?
zh: 我如何查看一个页面并确定接下来要发起哪些后续查询?

en: And then how do I analyze the set of results I have at the end and determine what could be relevant, which is a different relevance determination.
zh: 然后是我如何分析最后得到的那组结果,并确定什么可能是相关的,这是一种不同的相关性判断。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I think that set of tasks, which are fairly narrow, you can optimize for in isolation through a set of training examples.
zh: 所以我认为这组任务相当窄,你可以通过一组训练样本来单独地对它们进行优化。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so actually in training context one, we have a staged curriculum where early on in the life cycle of training, we only give it problems that are easier and need one to two hops to satisfy.
zh: 所以实际上在 context one 的训练中,我们有一个分阶段的课程,在训练生命周期的早期,我们只给它那些更容易的、需要一到两跳才能满足的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then later on, we start to like expand the difficulty of the tasks that it has.
zh: 然后在后期,我们开始扩展它所面对任务的难度。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then we also do two phases of training.
zh: 而且我们还做了两个阶段的训练。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's not only trained through reinforcement learning.

speaker: Unknown
en: We also have an additional supervised fine tuning stage, which uses synthetic data and data distilled from open weights models.

zh: 但你真正追求的是把模型落地到正确的一组先验上,即我在某些情况下应该如何表现。
